title: Unit 2 Stand-alone 4: Disuse Atrophy & Contracture Risk

question.stem: Complete the diagram by dragging from the choices below to specify what condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take to address that condition, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor to assess the client's progress.

bowtieActions.text: Implement scheduled passive and active-assistive range-of-motion exercises
Place the immobilized joint in continuous acute flexion without repositioning
Collaborate with physical therapy for progressive isometric muscle activation
Restrain all extremities to prevent involuntary muscular contractions

bowtieParams.text: Bilateral limb circumference measurements at reproducible landmarks
Passive and active joint angle range-of-motion (goniometry)

question.preamble: The rehabilitation nurse is planning care for a client who has experienced prolonged immobilization following traumatic orthopedic fixation.
question.explanation: Prolonged immobilization and lack of mechanical loading reduce metabolic demand and protein synthesis while upregulating the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, leading to accelerated degradation of myofibrillar proteins and disuse muscle atrophy (shrinkage of cell size and loss of muscle mass). To counteract atrophy and prevent irreversible joint contractures, the nurse implements scheduled range-of-motion exercises and collaborates with physical therapy for isometric and resistance training. Monitoring limb circumference and joint degrees of motion verifies recovery and prevents functional deterioration.

leftContent.intro: A 44-year-old client is admitted to the inpatient rehabilitation unit following 8 weeks of non-weight-bearing cast immobilization for a complex tibial plateau fracture.

tabs.title: Physical Therapy Assessment
tabs.content: Right Lower Extremity: Severe visible reduction in gastrocnemius and quadriceps bulk compared to left side; right mid-calf circumference 31 cm vs left mid-calf 37 cm; 3/5 motor strength; passive ankle dorsiflexion restricted to neutral (0 degrees). Skin intact without swelling or erythema.
